routes.description: Defend objective moral facts by treating clear moral appearances as defeasible grounds for belief, challenging desire-dependent accounts of reasons, and extending a priori knowledge of objective natures to moral relations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by establishing that appearances can provide prima facie justification, that explanationism does not defeat this entitlement, and that objective evaluative facts better account for practical reasons and paradigmatic moral judgments.

motionBridge.description: Connect justified appearances concerning badness and suffering to knowledge of objective moral facts.

centralBridges.description: Establish a defeasible entitlement to accept intellectual and perceptual appearances without requiring them to explain observations.
Show that desire-based theories cannot fully explain rational priority, consistency, and judgments about what agents have reason to do.
Defend a priori access to objective relations among things and extend that account to the relation between suffering and badness.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Argue that causal concepts and explanatory background beliefs ultimately depend on representational experience.
Explain how beliefs about objective value can organize emotions, desires, and morally guided conduct.

routes.description: Deny objective moral facts by grounding practical reasons in agents' desires and deliberative perspectives, while maintaining that experience supports belief through explanatory and causal relations that moral truths do not supply.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by showing that categorical moral reasons lack an intelligible basis, that moral propositions are unnecessary to explain moral experience, and that conceptual learning and moral motivation can be accounted for without objective moral facts.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of desire-independent categorical reasons and moral explanatory evidence to denial of objective moral facts and justified moral knowledge.

centralBridges.description: Ground practical reasons in desires, values, self-conception, and the deliberative perspective required for reasons to have practical purchase.
Require beliefs to receive evidential support through explanatory relations to experience and show that moral truth performs no necessary explanatory work.
Explain perceptual and a priori cognition through causal models, predictive refinement, and relations among concepts rather than foundational contentful appearances.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Account for moral judgment and conduct through projected antecedent values, emotions, and stable practical commitments.
Resolve the apparent conditional standoff by comparing the wider epistemological and metaphysical commitments of the competing views.

sections.title: Objective Moral Facts and Desire-Dependent Reasons
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal metaphysical clash over whether categorical moral reasons exist or whether practical reasons must derive from desires, values, and an agent's deliberative perspective.

sections.title: Appearances, Explanationism, and Moral Justification
sections.rationale: This issue directly addresses whether appearances provide prima facie justification or whether evidential support requires a best-explanation relation that moral propositions cannot supply.

sections.title: Representational Experience and Predictive Learning
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether explanationist background models presuppose accepted representational appearances or can emerge through causal learning and predictive refinement without such foundations.

sections.title: A Priori Knowledge, Analyticity, and Objective Natures
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether reflective seemings disclose only conceptual relations or can justify synthetic a priori knowledge of objective natures, including the badness of suffering.

sections.title: Moral Belief, Emotion, and Practical Conduct
sections.rationale: This issue concerns whether objective moral belief independently shapes motivation and emotion or instead projects antecedent values whose practical influence can survive error theory.
